title: Categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone: ECoG auditory oddball in 6 epilepsy patients (Si, Zhou & Hong 2017)
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six patients with medically intractable epilepsy who passively listened to a two-deviant auditory oddball sequence of synthesized Mandarin syllables. The paradigm used a tone continuum with a frequent standard, a cross-category deviant and a within-category deviant, allowing investigation of categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone. The data are reorganised into iEEG-BIDS without signal processing from a public Zenodo record.
methods_description: ECoG was recorded from subdural grid electrodes with a g.USBamp amplifier at 1200 Hz (0.1 Hz high-pass, 50 Hz notch). Patients watched a silent movie while hearing 500 trials (250 for S6) of a Mandarin /i/ tone oddball with an 1100 ms onset-to-onset interval and 5% jitter. Electrode placement was determined by clinical need only, and events were decoded from a trigger channel.
